task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of September 3, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper news update about Dunveil Museum's reversal of a proposed admission increase and how the institution now plans to address its budget gap.

facts.text: Dunveil Museum's trustees withdrew a planned admission increase on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026.
The standard admission charge for visitors age 16 and older will remain $8 rather than rising to $11 on Oct. 1; younger visitors enter free.
The increase had been announced July 23 but had not taken effect.
The museum's budget projection at the unchanged $8 admission price shows a $120,000 operating gap for the coming financial year, before the new gift and savings.
A newly confirmed unrestricted operating gift will contribute $70,000 toward that gap.
Trustees expect to save another $30,000 by closing the temporary-exhibition gallery on Wednesdays and reducing outside catalog printing.
The remaining projected gap is $20,000, and the museum has not identified a complete funding plan for it.
The permanent collection, reading room and cafe will remain open on Wednesdays under the revised schedule.
The temporary gallery's Wednesday closure begins Oct. 7 and will be reviewed after six months.
Director Elna Reed said no permanent posts will be cut under the announced savings plan, although casual gallery shifts will be reduced.
The museum has not yet published the number of casual hours affected.
Local tour organizer Pella Sorn said some prebooked Wednesday groups expected access to a temporary textile exhibition.
The museum will offer those groups an alternative date or a refund of their group-booking payment.
Sorn said, "An unchanged ticket price is useful news, but my visitors also need to know which doors will be open."
Reed said, "The gift lets us keep the entry price where it is. It does not remove every difficult choice in the budget."
The museum counted 42,600 visits last year, including free school visits and repeat admissions.
Those visits include free admissions and repeat visits, and the record does not specify how many paid the standard rate; multiplying all 42,600 by $3 would not establish foregone revenue.
The donor requested anonymity; the gift agreement supplied imposes no exhibition-theme requirement.
The museum occupies a former customs building and has charged the same adult price since 2021.
The trustees have not committed to keeping admission at $8 beyond the next financial year.
